documents.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence General Use Guidelines
documents.stance_why: The document is general GenAI guidance mostly about data and privacy and sets no course-level AI stance: it says 'Course instructors have the discretion to allow, prohibit, or put parameters around the use of GenAI', so the decision is handed to instructors.
documents.summary: UW-IT general use guidelines for GenAI stress approved tools, data classification, review of output, disclosure and recordkeeping, and compliance with policy. For coursework they only say students follow their course rules and instructors decide.

units.why: States the university's support for GenAI as a framework preamble: 'supports the responsible use of generative AI (GenAI) when helpful to further its mission'. It sets purpose and principle, so P56, with a permit position.
units.anchor: supports the responsible use of generative AI (GenAI) when helpful to further its mission

units.why: Says the guidelines are 'general advice for the UW community', not binding rules; this scopes the document, so P56 framework preamble fits best.
units.anchor: These guidelines provide general advice for the UW community

units.why: Restricts University data to approved services: 'Only UW-approved services and applications may be used with University data'. A rule to use approved tools, P92, rather than a review process (P65).
units.anchor: Only UW-approved services and applications may be used with University data

units.why: Warns that unapproved tools and unauthorized data release 'could result in violations of policy or law', a consequence tied to compliance with policy and law, P77.
units.anchor: could result in violations of policy or law for which you or the University may

units.why: Says UWIT 'can review tools and use cases' to inform unit decisions on approval, which describes institutional review and approval of AI tools, P65.
units.anchor: UWIT can review tools and use cases to help inform unit decisions

units.why: Points to the list of 'GenAI tools approved and supported by UWIT'. A pointer to know the approved list, P92.
units.anchor: GenAI tools approved and supported by UWIT

units.why: Requires that all GenAI use 'must comply with all relevant UW policies and standards': P77 comply with existing policy.
units.anchor: All use of GenAI must comply with all relevant UW policies and standards

units.why: Offers 'Complimentary training, tool review, architectural guidance, and security assessments': institutional AI training and support for the community, P70.
units.anchor: Complimentary training, tool review, architectural guidance, and security assessments are available
units.fit_note: Also covers tool review and security assessments, not only training.

units.why: States 'You are ultimately responsible and accountable for your use of GenAI and all outcomes derived from it', a user-accountability rule; P29 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: You are ultimately responsible and accountable for your use of GenAI
units.fit_note: Applies to all uses and outcomes, not only submitted work.

units.why: Says the Appropriate Use Policy and security/privacy policies 'apply to the use of all technologies, including GenAI': existing policy applies, P77.
units.anchor: apply to the use of all technologies, including GenAI

units.why: Tells students 'Students must adhere to policies and rules applicable to their course or project': P78 students follow each course's rules.
units.anchor: Students must adhere to policies and rules applicable to their course or project

units.why: States 'Course instructors have the discretion to allow, prohibit, or put parameters around the use of GenAI', which hands the decision to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: Course instructors have the discretion to allow, prohibit, or put parameters around the use of

units.why: Requires 'You must review GenAI output before using or publishing it': verification of AI output, P31.
units.anchor: You must review GenAI output before using or publishing it

units.why: Says GenAI 'may enhance, but does not replace, human judgment, particularly in decision-making affecting individuals': humans stay responsible for decisions about people, P73.
units.anchor: may enhance, but does not replace, human judgment

units.why: Asks users to 'Avoid GenAI use that may reinforce inappropriate biases or create barriers for underrepresented groups': bias and harms, P53.
units.anchor: Avoid GenAI use that may reinforce inappropriate biases

units.why: Says 'Disclosing GenAI use is often advisable and may be mandatory' and nondisclosure 'may have serious consequences ... in coursework'. Disclosure with each submission, P24; P28 not chosen because no rule on penalizing disclosed use is stated.
units.anchor: Disclosing GenAI use is often advisable and may be mandatory

units.why: Requires 'detailed records of GenAI use, especially when personal data is involved': keep logs, P26.
units.anchor: Maintain detailed records of GenAI use, especially when personal data is involved
units.fit_note: Recordkeeping for compliance and privacy, not necessarily submitted to an instructor.

units.why: Directs users to 'Document relevant processes in the TrustArc personal data inventory', an administrative registration duty that no existing type captures.
units.anchor: Document relevant processes in the TrustArc personal data inventory
units.uncovered_note: Users must register GenAI processes that involve personal data in the university's personal data inventory.

units.why: Requires 'compliance with records protection and preservation laws': comply with law, P77.
units.anchor: Ensure compliance with records protection and preservation laws

units.why: Allows only public data: 'Data intended for public consumption (classification Level 1) can be used with GenAI'; protect data, P50.
units.anchor: Data intended for public consumption

units.why: Bans restricted data: 'Do not use data that is restricted (Level 2 through Level 4), unless appropriate security and privacy controls' exist. Protect confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: Do not use data that is restricted

units.why: For high-risk uses 'like hiring, admissions, or performance evaluations', users contact the privacy office for an impact assessment: a review of AI use before deployment, P65.
units.anchor: high-risk processes like hiring, admissions, or performance evaluations
units.fit_note: A privacy impact assessment for a specific use, not purchase or deployment of a tool.

units.why: Lists the UW AI Task Force, Town Halls and Speaker Series: community engagement on AI, P88.
units.anchor: UW AI Task Force, Town Halls, and AI Perspectives Speaker Series

units.why: Says 'Report suspected security and privacy incidents immediately' with contacts: a duty to report data exposure, P71.
units.anchor: Report suspected security and privacy incidents immediately

documents.unit: Teaching@UW / Center for Teaching and Learning
documents.title: Sample AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Some AI use in the assignment
No AI use in the assignment
documents.stance_why: The page states 'there is no single university-wide UW AI policy' and supplies sample conditional-use and no-AI statements that instructors 'can adapt'; it sets no stance itself and offers named templates, so delegates.
documents.summary: Teaching@UW page with sample course-level and assignment-level AI syllabus statements (conditional use, no AI, some AI, no AI in assignment) and drafting prompts. It stresses disclosure, verification, privacy and instructor choice.

units.why: States the page's purpose: 'examples you can adapt to articulate your expectations for whether and how students may use AI'. Leaves the choice to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: examples you can adapt to articulate your expectations for whether and how students may use

units.why: Says to state expectations 'in both the syllabus and assignment instructions' so students avoid unauthorized use: a call for syllabus AI statements, P09.
units.anchor: Stating your expectations in both the syllabus and assignment instructions

units.why: States 'there is no single university-wide UW AI policy' and that expectations clarify 'how your course might differ from other courses'. This is a per-course scope statement, P11; the recommendation to communicate is covered by the P09 unit above.
units.anchor: there is no single university-wide UW AI policy
units.fit_note: Also recommends discussing expectations in the syllabus and on the first day.

units.why: Offers 'two basic types of AI-related course policy: conditional use ... and prohibiting any AI use': named categories of course policy, P05.
units.anchor: two basic types of AI-related course policy

units.why: Says conditional use 'structures AI use so that it supports, rather than undermines, student learning': a learning-based reason for allowing AI conditionally, nearest P83.
units.anchor: structures AI use so that it supports, rather than undermines, student learning
units.fit_note: States a learning purpose for conditional use without tying it to stated learning objectives.

units.why: The sample statement says AI 'can also impede your development of critical thinking, reasoning, and communication skills': AI shortcuts skill-building, P41.
units.anchor: they can also impede your development of critical thinking, reasoning, and communication skills

units.why: The sample says AI is permitted 'to help you learn how to leverage these tools professionally': professional-skill rationale, P44.
units.anchor: to help you learn how to leverage these tools professionally

units.why: The sample permits AI only in listed work: 'AI use is permitted in specific assignments and activities'. Permission is set per assignment, P04.
units.anchor: AI use is permitted in specific assignments and activities
units.fit_note: Permission is decided per assignment in the sample statement.

units.why: The sample tells students to 'Pay attention to assignment instructions for information about whether and how you may use AI': follow each assignment's rules, P78.
units.anchor: Pay attention to assignment instructions for information about whether and how you may use AI

units.why: The sample says 'Using AI in other ways will be considered academic misconduct': a fallback rule that unlisted uses are banned. P06 chosen over P36 because it defines what applies outside the listed uses.
units.anchor: Using AI in other ways will be considered academic misconduct
units.fit_note: The fallback is expressed as academic misconduct.

units.why: The sample invites students with questions to 'please contact me': ask the instructor, P10.
units.anchor: if you have any questions about this policy, please contact me

units.why: The sample warns 'AI results can be biased and inaccurate. It is your responsibility to ensure that the information you use from AI is accurate': verify output, P31.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to ensure that the information you use from AI is accurate

units.why: The sample warns students not to 'share copyrighted materials, original work, or personal information' because tools reuse data: P49 no uploading protected works.
units.anchor: be careful not to share copyrighted materials, original work, or personal information
units.fit_note: Also covers personal information.

units.why: The no-AI sample says 'Using AI tools may limit your capacity to develop these skills': skill-building rationale for the ban, P41.
units.anchor: Using AI tools may limit your capacity to develop these skills

units.why: The no-AI sample: 'all work submitted for this course must be your own. Any use of AI tools will be considered academic misconduct': a default ban on all work, P01.
units.anchor: Any use of AI tools will be considered academic misconduct

units.why: Tells instructors 'no technology can reliably identify unauthorized student use of AI': detection is unreliable, P39.
units.anchor: no technology can reliably identify unauthorized student use of AI

units.why: States 'instructors have the right to prohibit the use of AI tools', affirming instructor authority, P04.
units.anchor: instructors have the right to prohibit the use of AI tools

units.why: Invites 'students into the process of defining your course's AI policy' through community agreements: co-create the policy, P67.
units.anchor: Inviting students into the process of defining your course's AI policy

units.why: Says assignment-level expectations 'foster a culture of academic integrity by providing students with more clarity': a call for assignment-level statements, P09.
units.anchor: Articulating your expectations regarding AI use in assignment instructions

units.why: The some-AI template: 'you may use AI tools to [insert tasks]. AI tools may not be used to [insert tasks]': per-assignment lists of allowed and disallowed tasks, P04.
units.anchor: you may use AI tools to [insert tasks]. AI tools may not be used to
units.fit_note: Template for per-assignment lists of allowed and disallowed tasks.

units.why: The template requires students to 'briefly (1-2 sentences) identify the tool you used and describe how you used it, and how you evaluated, modified, and verified': disclosure of tool and use, P25.
units.anchor: identify the tool you used and describe how you used it
units.fit_note: Includes describing evaluation and verification, not the prompt or output.

units.why: The template says 'Failure to disclose AI use will be considered a violation of academic integrity standards': nondisclosure is the violation, P28.
units.anchor: Failure to disclose AI use will be considered a violation of academic integrity standards

units.why: The template asks instructors to give 'an example of how I would like you to disclose your use of AI': communicating disclosure expectations, P24.
units.anchor: Here is an example of how I would like you to disclose your use of

units.why: The UW Bothell example has students later use 'UW Copilot as your research partner' to develop a question after no-AI topic generation: a named university tool for one assignment, P17.
units.anchor: reviewed with UW Copilot as your research partner
units.fit_note: The assignment names UW Copilot for refining the question; the tool is institution-wide.

units.why: The same example says 'Instead of using AI to brainstorm for you, you will be the researcher': brainstorming is excluded so the student stays the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: Instead of using AI to brainstorm for you
units.fit_note: A specific no-AI-brainstorming rule for one assignment.

units.why: Advises instructors to 'explain to students why not using AI in the assignment benefits them': give reasons for the rules, P66.
units.anchor: explain to students why not using AI in the assignment benefits them

units.why: The no-AI assignment template: 'Because AI tools can replace rather than support this learning process, their use is not permitted for this assignment': an assignment-level ban, P01.
units.anchor: their use is not permitted for this assignment
units.fit_note: Assignment-level rather than course-level ban.

units.why: The template says 'please consult with me before using it' when unsure whether a tool counts as generative AI or is permitted: ask first, P10.
units.anchor: please consult with me before using it

units.why: Lists elements instructors should consider when drafting their own policy (how, why, consequences, questions): a drafting checklist, P09.
units.anchor: Consider the following as you begin the process of drafting your own policy
units.fit_note: A drafting checklist rather than a requirement to include a statement.

units.why: Prompts instructors with 'What steps should students take to document their AI use?': documentation of AI use, P26.
units.anchor: What steps should students take to document their AI use?
units.fit_note: Prompts instructors to define documentation steps.

units.why: Prompts 'How do your expectations relate to students' learning?': ties AI rules to learning, P83.
units.anchor: How do your expectations relate to students' learning?
units.fit_note: Links expectations to student learning generally.

units.why: Prompts 'How will you respond if students do not comply with your expectations?': decide consequences in advance, P37.
units.anchor: How will you respond if students do not comply with your expectations?
units.fit_note: Prompts instructors to decide consequences without naming any.

units.why: Names two UW-supported tools 'freely available to most UW students, staff, and faculty': Microsoft Copilot and Purple. Institution-wide licensed tools, P92 rather than P17.
units.anchor: two UW-supported generative AI tools freely available to most UW students, staff, and faculty
units.fit_note: Notes the tools are free, which also relates to access.

units.why: Tells instructors who 'plan to require students to use generative AI' to 'consider the data privacy implications of the tools you assign': prefer vetted tools, P50.
units.anchor: consider the data privacy implications of the tools you assign

units.why: The phrase 'If you plan to require students to use generative AI' shows instructors may require AI use in a course: P79.
units.anchor: If you plan to require students to use generative AI
units.fit_note: Only implies instructors may require AI; the sentence is conditional.

units.why: Describes a SEED-AI pilot of 'an online, self-paced tool to support UW instructors as they draft or revise AI policies': faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: piloting an online, self-paced tool to support UW instructors

units.why: States 'Students are expected to practice high standards of academic and professional honesty and integrity': an integrity-based expectation, P95.
units.anchor: Students are expected to practice high standards of academic and professional honesty and integrity

units.why: Says the University communicates 'the importance of knowing and understanding the expectations of both the University and specific instructors': students learn each course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: knowing and understanding the expectations of both the University and specific instructors

units.why: Tells instructors who suspect misconduct they 'can make a report to your campus Student Conduct office': the formal reporting step, P81.
units.anchor: you can make a report to your campus Student Conduct office

documents.unit: Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
documents.title: AI for Support and Growth
documents.stance_why: The policy says 'AI is not allowed on any graded assignment that is not included in the authorized list' while permitting AI for general questions and ungraded work, so AI is banned on graded work unless explicitly authorized.
documents.summary: A template-like Allen School policy that permits AI for ungraded work and for graded work listed as authorized, with data privacy rules, attribution, and referral of misuse to CSSC. It reads as a shared template that instructors fill in.

units.why: The overview sets a default for ungraded work: 'You may use AI for general course questions and ungraded work'. Closest is the tutor-for-understanding type, P12.
units.anchor: You may use AI for general course questions and ungraded work
units.fit_note: Covers ungraded work generally, not only concept understanding.

units.why: 'AI is not allowed on any graded assignment that is not included in the authorized list' is the fallback ban when an assignment is unlisted, P06.
units.anchor: AI is not allowed on any graded assignment that is not included in the authorized
units.fit_note: The default is a ban on graded work except as listed, which is also close to P01.

units.why: 'You may also use AI on graded work when that work is specifically listed in Authorized Graded Work': permission set by an instructor-filled list, P04.
units.anchor: when that work is specifically listed in Authorized Graded Work
units.fit_note: Per-assignment authorization through a list the instructor fills in.

units.why: 'Read the full policy carefully before using AI': students learn the rules, P78.
units.anchor: Read the full policy carefully before using AI

units.why: Defines AI as 'generative AI systems that can produce or modify text, code, images, audio, video, or other content', naming chatbots and agents: P61.
units.anchor: generative AI systems that can produce or modify text, code, images, audio, video, or other

units.why: The definition includes AI 'built into IDEs, operating systems, or browsers when they generate or substantially rewrite content': covers embedded AI, P07.
units.anchor: AI features built into IDEs, operating systems, or browsers

units.why: The definition 'excludes non-generative tools such as basic spell-check, grammar/syntax highlighting, and linters': routine features exempt, P100.
units.anchor: excludes non-generative tools such as basic spell-check, grammar/syntax highlighting, and linters

units.why: Rationale: 'AI can be valuable for exploring concepts, practicing skills, and developing one's capabilities': benefits of AI for learning, P87.
units.anchor: AI can be valuable for exploring concepts, practicing skills, and developing one's capabilities

units.why: 'AI use is allowed on some assignments to give you experience working with these tools': experience with AI as a skill, P44.
units.anchor: to give you experience working with these tools
units.fit_note: Framed as experience that supplements knowledge, not explicitly as a career skill.

units.why: 'some assignments will require you to demonstrate your knowledge and skills without the use of AI': learning rationale for unassisted work, P41.
units.anchor: some assignments will require you to demonstrate your knowledge and skills without the use of
units.fit_note: Also says students are responsible for their own learning.

units.why: The Authorized Graded Work section says 'AI use is permitted only for the following graded work' and leaves blanks for the instructor, P04.
units.anchor: AI use is permitted only for the following graded work
units.fit_note: The instructor fills in the authorized assignments.

units.why: 'The instructor may provide additional instructions or limits for any authorized activity': conditions set per activity, P04.
units.anchor: The instructor may provide additional instructions or limits for any authorized activity

units.why: Permitted Actions: 'general questions and support-including concept explanations, study questions, practice problems, ungraded exercises, and exploratory coding-on all work': tutor use, P12.
units.anchor: concept explanations, study questions, practice problems, ungraded exercises, and exploratory coding
units.fit_note: Also includes practice problems and exploratory coding (P14, P15).

units.why: 'You may use AI to help develop your submissions only for the specific assignments listed': AI-produced submission work under stated conditions, P16.
units.anchor: only for the specific assignments listed in Authorized Graded Work
units.fit_note: Allows AI help on submissions for listed assignments, subject to limits; not specific to code.

units.why: 'Do not use AI to produce work you submit on any graded assignment that is not listed': do not have AI produce submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: Do not use AI to produce work you submit on any graded assignment

units.why: 'Do not use AI in ways that exceed the stated limits for an authorized graded activity': stay within instructor limits, closest P04.
units.anchor: Do not use AI in ways that exceed the stated limits
units.fit_note: Rule that students stay within the instructor's per-activity limits.

units.why: 'Do not submit AI-generated work, or lightly edited AI-generated work, as your own' when independence is required: P19.
units.anchor: Do not submit AI-generated work, or lightly edited AI-generated work, as your own

units.why: 'If an assignment has stricter rules, those rules override this policy for that assignment': assignment rules take precedence, P04.
units.anchor: If an assignment has stricter rules, those rules override this policy for that assignment
units.fit_note: Precedence rule for stricter assignment-level rules.

units.why: Example: 'Not allowed: using AI to fix a bug or rewrite a proof for you' on unlisted work: no AI debugging of graded work, P21.
units.anchor: using AI to fix a bug or rewrite a proof for you

units.why: Example: 'Allowed: using AI to explain a concept, generate practice questions, or help you study for a quiz': tutor and study aids, P14.
units.anchor: using AI to explain a concept, generate practice questions, or help you study for a

units.why: Example: 'Allowed: using AI on an ungraded practice exercise or exploratory code that will not be submitted': practice use, P14.
units.anchor: using AI on an ungraded practice exercise or exploratory code

units.why: Example: 'Allowed: using AI to help produce your submission on a graded assignment if that activity is listed': P16.
units.anchor: using AI to help produce your submission on a graded assignment if that activity is
units.fit_note: Not specific to code; allows AI-produced submissions on listed work.

units.why: Example: 'Not allowed: copying work produced by an AI into your submission' on unlisted work: P19.
units.anchor: copying work produced by an AI into your submission

units.why: 'specify the tool you used and how you utilized it in your work' on authorized assignments: disclosure of tool and use, P25.
units.anchor: specify the tool you used and how you utilized it in your work
units.fit_note: Tool and use described; prompts and outputs are not required.

units.why: 'Before using AI on graded work, confirm that the activity is listed': check the rules first, P78.
units.anchor: confirm that the activity is listed under Authorized Graded Work

units.why: 'Use AI to expand your thinking, not to replace it': the student stays the thinker, P32.
units.anchor: Use AI to expand your thinking, not to replace it

units.why: 'Verify AI output carefully; AI can be inaccurate, incomplete, biased': P31.
units.anchor: Verify AI output carefully; AI can be inaccurate, incomplete, biased

units.why: 'you should be able to explain and defend every part of what you submit': P30.
units.anchor: you should be able to explain and defend every part of what you submit

units.why: 'When in doubt, err on the side of not using AI and ask the course staff': P10.
units.anchor: err on the side of not using AI and ask the course staff for clarification

units.why: 'Do not upload course-specific materials-including assignment prompts, course code, datasets, class notes, hidden tests, solution keys': P49 chosen over P20 because it covers notes and keys, not only specs and own code.
units.anchor: Do not upload course-specific materials

units.why: Warns that agents like Cursor and Claude Code 'can automatically access files beyond what you explicitly share': autonomous coding agents, P07.
units.anchor: can automatically access files beyond what you explicitly share
units.fit_note: Concerns file access by agents rather than whether agents may be used.

units.why: 'confirm what it can access and restrict or scope that access so it does not read private repositories, hidden test files': P07, requiring scoping of agent access.
units.anchor: confirm what it can access and restrict or scope that access
units.fit_note: Requires scoping agent access instead of disabling the agent.

units.why: 'Do not submit personal, sensitive, or university-protected information into AI tools': P50.
units.anchor: Do not submit personal, sensitive, or university-protected information into AI tools

units.why: 'prompts and outputs may be stored or reused by third-party AI providers': AI tools store prompts, P50.
units.anchor: prompts and outputs may be stored or reused by third-party AI providers

units.why: 'using Purple or Allen School-provided tools is advised': sanctioned tools with stronger privacy, P17.
units.anchor: using Purple or Allen School-provided tools is advised if possible

units.why: 'Using AI in ways prohibited ... will be considered academic misconduct and referred to CSSC': misconduct with referral, P36.
units.anchor: will be considered academic misconduct and referred to CSSC

units.why: 'receive no credit for the affected assignment. Stronger penalties, up to and including failing the course': concrete penalties, P37.
units.anchor: at minimum, receive no credit for the affected assignment

units.why: 'In cases of group work, all students will be held equally responsible' unless clear evidence shows otherwise: group responsibility, no existing type covers it.
units.anchor: all students will be held equally responsible for violation
units.uncovered_note: In group work, all team members are equally responsible for an AI violation unless clear evidence shows some were uninvolved.

units.why: 'Students with accessibility needs or other extenuating circumstances should contact the instructor to discuss exceptions': accommodations, P51.
units.anchor: should contact the instructor to discuss exceptions
units.fit_note: Exceptions for accessibility and circumstances, not about cost.

units.why: 'Accommodations or exceptions require instructor approval before they are used': exceptions process, P80.
units.anchor: Accommodations or exceptions require instructor approval before they are used

documents.unit: Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
documents.title: Guidelines for Use of Artificial Intelligence in Research (Schoolwide Policies page)
documents.stance_why: The research guidelines say 'If and when AI is used in research, it must be used responsibly' and set accuracy, privacy and disclosure conditions without banning AI, so permit with conditions; they cover research, not coursework.
documents.summary: Allen School guidance for AI in research: authors are accountable for accuracy, should not upload confidential data or manuscripts, and are strongly encouraged to disclose AI use to co-authors and advisors. It does not address coursework.

units.why: Says AI in research 'must be used responsibly' across all aspects of the research process: scope and principle for research, P62.
units.anchor: when AI is used in research, it must be used responsibly

units.why: 'Human authors remain fully responsible for the integrity of their work': P29.
units.anchor: Human authors remain fully responsible for the integrity of their work

units.why: Says 'norms governing the use of AI in research ... are evolving': the guidance is provisional, P54.
units.anchor: norms governing the use of AI in research
units.fit_note: Says norms are evolving rather than that the page will be revised.

units.why: 'Authors are fully responsible for the accuracy and originality of their work': P29.
units.anchor: Authors are fully responsible for the accuracy and originality of their work

units.why: 'Generative AI tools can produce incorrect statements, fabricated citations': verify output, P31.
units.anchor: Generative AI tools can produce incorrect statements, fabricated citations

units.why: 'Submitting or posting work that includes these errors may constitute research misconduct': misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: may constitute research misconduct
units.fit_note: Research misconduct rather than coursework integrity.

units.why: 'you should inform your co-authors and ensure that all content is carefully verified': disclosure to co-authors plus verification, P24.
units.anchor: you should inform your co-authors and ensure that all content is carefully verified
units.fit_note: Disclosure is to co-authors, not with a submission.

units.why: 'Before uploading any data, code, or text, you should consult your research mentor': data upload caution, P50.
units.anchor: Before uploading any data, code, or text, you should consult your research mentor

units.why: Lists sensitive data whose disclosure through AI is a risk (HIPAA, FERPA, human subjects, NDA, university IP): protect confidential data, P50.
units.anchor: unintended disclosure of sensitive or restricted information

units.why: Peer review: 'you must not upload submitted or unpublished manuscripts to external AI tools unless explicitly permitted by the venue': P62.
units.anchor: you must not upload submitted or unpublished manuscripts to external AI tools

units.why: 'You are responsible for understanding and following the policies of the venue you are reviewing for': defers to the venue, P62.
units.anchor: understanding and following the policies of the venue

units.why: 'We also strongly recommend disclosing all AI usage (other than minor editing) in your research outputs': P24.
units.anchor: strongly recommend disclosing all AI usage (other than minor editing)

units.why: 'Disclosure can typically be included in the acknowledgments or methods section': where to state AI use, P27.
units.anchor: Disclosure can typically be included in the acknowledgments or methods section
units.fit_note: Placement in acknowledgments or methods rather than at the code location.

units.why: 'make sure that your collaborators and coauthors are fully aware of the methods used': disclosure to collaborators, P24.
units.anchor: make sure that your collaborators and coauthors are fully aware of the methods

units.why: 'Students are expected to discuss AI usage with their advisors and to proactively disclose': disclosure to advisors, P24.
units.anchor: proactively disclose how generative AI tools are being used
units.fit_note: Disclosure to advisors in research.

units.why: 'Expectations are likely to vary across research groups': permission varies by group, closest P04.
units.anchor: Expectations are likely to vary across research groups
units.fit_note: Varies by research group rather than by instructor.

units.why: 'Authors are expected to understand the content of every paper they cite and every claim they include': understand what you submit, P30.
units.anchor: understand the content of every paper they cite and every claim

documents.title: Academic integrity (general policies), generative AI paragraph
documents.stance_why: The paragraph says the university has no overarching policy and 'The College of Engineering, likewise, defers to the judgement of the instructor', so the decision is handed to instructors.
documents.summary: A short College of Engineering paragraph saying there is no university or college AI policy and that instructors should be deliberate and clear. It suggests students keep process records and be reminded they remain accountable.

units.why: 'The University of Washington has no overarching policy on student use of generative AI': no university-wide stance, so decisions fall to instructors, P04.
units.anchor: no overarching policy on student use of generative AI
units.fit_note: States the absence of a university policy.

units.why: 'The College of Engineering, likewise, defers to the judgement of the instructor': P04.
units.anchor: defers to the judgement of the instructor

units.why: Says Teaching@UW 'maintains a guidance page regarding teaching and AI': a pointer to faculty support, P63.
units.anchor: Teaching@UW maintains a guidance page

units.why: 'Instructors are encouraged to be deliberate and clear in course guidelines': a call for explicit course AI statements, P09.
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to be deliberate and clear in course guidelines

units.why: 'It may be reasonable to prohibit all use of generative AI in one course but allow specific usages in another, depending on course learning objectives': learning objectives drive the rule, P83.
units.anchor: depending on course learning objectives
units.fit_note: Also says rules may differ between courses (P11).

units.why: 'Encourage students to save records of their progress over time (e.g., intermediate products, logs of work process)': process records, P26.
units.anchor: Encourage students to save records of their progress over time
units.fit_note: Records of the work process to protect students if AI is banned, not records of AI use.

units.why: 'An engineer uses tools responsibly and knows they are accountable for their own work output regardless of their tools': students own their work, P29.
units.anchor: accountable for their own work output regardless of their tools

units.why: 'It may be appropriate for some tasks in some contexts and not others': AI suitability depends on task and context, P04.
units.anchor: It may be appropriate for some tasks in some contexts and not others

notes: Coder A. Course layer deferred in collect. The Allen School 'AI for Support and Growth' doc is a template with blank authorized-work placeholders; the research guidelines cover research only.
